purpose: Bind the arithmetic that is unique to the AggressiveV4 opportunity model, so a later Rust port agrees with Android by measurement rather than by re-reading the same prose.

provenance.derivation: Hand-computed from the constants and formulas in apps/android/core/.../engine/OpportunityEngine.kt and the plan text, and written down before the Kotlin validator was run. This file is NOT a dump of Kotlin output.
provenance.why_it_matters: market-regime-fit-v1.json can forbid regeneration because Rust is the source of its numbers. V4 has no second implementation yet, so nothing outside this file can catch Kotlin from agreeing with itself. Hand derivation is the only independence available, and it is what makes the first cross-language comparison a real one. Regenerating any expected value from Kotlin destroys that and must not be done.

units._hundredths suffix: the real value times 100, rounded to the nearest integer
units.multiples: hundredths, so 2000 is a multiple of 20.00

notes: Intermediates are carried as hundredths, not as floating-point literals. A port that computes 0.9480519480519481 and a port that computes 0.9480519480519480 are both correct, and a JSON float would make one of them fail.

No case is allowed to land on a .5 rounding boundary. Kotlin's roundToInt is half-up and Rust's f64::round is half-away-from-zero, and they disagree on negative halves. That difference is real but it is not what this contract is about, so no case may depend on it.

Two fundamentals cases sit exactly on a ramp anchor, which binds smoothRamp's inclusive comparisons: forward_pe at the sector low binds `observed <= lower`, ev_ebitda at the sector high binds `observed >= upper`. Both are still discriminating because the OTHER anchor is what moves them: forward_pe at 0.7x separates V4_FUND_SECTOR_CHEAP_MULT, ev_ebitda at 1.5x separates V4_FUND_SECTOR_RICH_MULT.

The two return-on-equity cases sit strictly INSIDE the band, and that is not a stylistic difference from the multiple cases. Its band is additive, so what a case must measure is a WIDTH, and an observation pinned on an edge measures only the edge it sits on: it returns -1.0 or +1.0 under the additive rule and under a multiplicative one alike. A first draft of this contract pinned ROE at its floor, and a mutation replacing the additive upper offset with the multiplicative one survived it. That is why both ROE cases are unpinned and why there are two of them, one on each side of the centre.

expected_without_benchmarks re-scores the SAME inputs with sector_benchmarks withheld. It is not decoration: without it a port that ignored the benchmark entirely could still pass, because a value can score the same under both rules by accident. Every pair below is chosen so the two readings differ in the score, and most also differ in the signal suffix.

composite_cases.name: four buckets in exact agreement earn the full bonus
three buckets close together, before the fourth arrives
composite_cases.binds: the control reading for the case below; odd-count median; a partial bonus

composite_cases.name: a fourth bucket that dissents lowers the score although it raises the count
composite_cases.binds: the SNDK defect. V3's bonus would rise from +10 to +15 on arrival; V4's falls, because the arriving bucket disagrees.

composite_cases.name: a spread past V4_SPREAD_FULL pays nothing at all
composite_cases.binds: the clamp on spread / V4_SPREAD_FULL. The raw ratio here is 1.0389, so a port that forgot to clamp would produce a negative bonus and a composite of 20 minus something.

composite_cases.name: two buckets, an even median and a single bonus step
composite_cases.binds: medianOf on an even count is the midpoint of the middle pair, not the lower of the two; (n - 1) = 1

composite_cases.name: no bucket reported
composite_cases.binds: the composite is 0 and there is no agreement reading, rather than a fabricated centre

composite_cases.name: beta at the low anchor haircuts nothing
composite_cases.binds: v3BetaRiskHaircut at V3_BETA_LOW_MILLIS is 0, so the haircut is applied and is zero — not skipped

composite_cases.name: beta midway up the ramp haircuts half the maximum
composite_cases.binds: smoothRamp is linear between the anchors; ((ramp + 1) / 2) * V3_BETA_HAIRCUT_MAX

composite_cases.name: beta at the high anchor haircuts the maximum
the regime's haircut multiplier is clamped at V3_BETA_HAIRCUT_MULT_MAX
composite_cases.binds: a multiplier of 4.0 must act as 2.5. Unclamped it would take 40 points and land the composite at 15.

composite_cases.name: the composite is bounded below, and only the haircut can reach that bound
composite_cases.binds: V4_COMPOSITE_BOUND on the negative side. The bonus is never negative and the centre never below -100, so -110 is unreachable without the haircut; here base - haircut is -125.

fundamentals_cases.name: forward P/E read against a sector that trades at 20x
fundamentals_cases.binds: the multiplicative sector band, V4_FUND_SECTOR_CHEAP_MULT. 14.00 sits exactly on 0.7 x 20.00, so the ramp pins at cheap; the absolute band calls the same multiple merely good.

fundamentals_cases.name: EV/EBITDA read against a sector that trades at 10x
fundamentals_cases.binds: V4_FUND_SECTOR_RICH_MULT. 15.00 sits exactly on 1.5 x 10.00, so the ramp pins at rich; the absolute band, which runs to 20.00, calls the same multiple middling.

fundamentals_cases.name: price to book read against a sector that trades at 4x
fundamentals_cases.binds: the sector band inverting the absolute verdict. 2.80 is dear against an absolute band that ends at 5.00 and cheap inside a sector at 4.00.

fundamentals_cases.name: return on equity above a sector earning 10%
fundamentals_cases.binds: the ADDITIVE band, which is the one field whose band has a different shape. 20% ROE tops out the absolute 0..20% band and is merely good inside a sector at 10%. It sits strictly INSIDE [centre - 500, centre + 1500], which is the point: a case pinned on either edge would score the same under a multiplicative band and would measure only the edge it sat on.

fundamentals_cases.name: return on equity below a sector earning 10%
fundamentals_cases.binds: V4_FUND_SECTOR_ROE_LOWER_OFFSET_BPS from the other side, and also strictly inside the band. 6% ROE is mediocre against the absolute band and near the floor of a sector at 10%. Both ROE cases are unpinned on purpose — the offsets are a width, and a width cannot be measured from an observation sitting on its edge.

fundamentals_cases.name: a shrinking share count is a buyback and scores positive
fundamentals_cases.binds: V4_FUND_SHARE_COUNT_WEIGHT and the sign. -3.00% is exactly V4_FUND_SHARE_COUNT_SHRINK_BPS, so the ramp pins.

fundamentals_cases.name: a growing share count is dilution and scores negative
fundamentals_cases.binds: the other side of the same ramp, so the sign is a measured claim and not a reading of the minus in the source

fundamentals_cases.name: a single-point share series contributes nothing, and nothing is not zero
fundamentals_cases.binds: one point cannot say which way the count moved. The term must be absent, so the bucket reports no evidence at all rather than a neutral score — a zero here would be a claim the data cannot support.
